svg.title: BSS commercial ownership and tenant-scoped RBAC
svg.desc: Proposed boundaries: a BSS Accounts gear owns legal-party identity, billing accounts, billing arrangements recorded as a payer-owned offer and a buyer-owned acceptance, account-use grants issued in one authorizing transaction, and issuer bindings. Contracts owns negotiated seller/issuer and buyer/debtor terms. Orders and Orders Workflow admit purchases only on grant evidence and hand one subscription with a common period and chain version to Subscriptions. Rating, Invoicing and Ledger value metered usage once per authorized leg and keep one result, document and entry per leg. The shared platform (Account Management, RBAC/PDP/PEP/SecureORM) works without BSS. No implementation implied.
svg.text: Proposed BSS ownership · Tenant-scoped RBAC · No implementation implied
Owns no consent, grants or accounts
Buyer-owned orders; attachment orders add legs, never services
Provisional intent → authorize_use → admission on grant evidence
Workflow coordinates conditional preparations and confirmations
Subscriptions owns one subscription, common period, chain version
Usage metered once; valued once per authorized leg grain
Per-leg results and postings; grouped invoice lines
Payer from grant and assignment, never from the tenant tree
Ledger resolves and pins books; Invoicing snapshots party profiles
All BSS components use the shared platform below. Consent, grants and event delivery alone grant no user access.
Tenant identity, status and organizational hierarchy
Billing actor aggregates hierarchy under barrier policy;
declares no BSS commercial ownership rule
Tenant-scoped permissions and enforced query constraints
Current views validated freshly per request, page and export
